With p=0 and q=0 it is plain preferential attachment, a tree of 7 edges; with p=0.4 some steps add edges between existing nodes instead, giving 12 edges and 7 triangles; with q=0.4 some steps rewire an existing edge instead, so the count stays at 7 and here one node is left with no edges." width="100%"} Starts from `m` isolated nodes and repeats one of three steps until there are `n` nodes: - with probability `p`, add `m` new edges, each from a random node to one chosen by preferential attachment - with probability `q`, rewire `m` edges: a random node drops one of its edges and links to a node chosen by preferential attachment instead - otherwise (probability `1 - p - q`), add a new node with `m` edges to existing nodes chosen by preferential attachment Preferential attachment chooses a node with probability proportional to its degree plus one, so isolated nodes can still be picked. Adding edges makes the graph denser, while rewiring moves links toward the hubs. A step that can't be carried out (no room for `m` more edges, or too few edges to rewire) adds a node instead. With `p = q = 0` this is plain preferential-attachment growth from `m` isolated nodes. The process follows NetworkX's `extended_barabasi_albert_graph()`. Because edges are also added between existing nodes and rewired, they have no natural direction: in a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Extended Barabási-Albert graphs are useful for: - modeling networks that grow both by newcomers and by new links among existing members - tuning the degree exponent and density of a scale-free graph through `p=` and `q=` - studying how rewiring toward hubs changes robustness and spreading ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. Must be greater than `m=`. [m]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of edges added, rewired, or attached to a new node in each step. Must be at least `1`. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of a step that adds edges between existing nodes, between `0` and `1`. [q]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of a step that rewires edges, between `0` and `1`. `p + q` must be less than `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `m=` is less than `1` or not less than `n=`, `p=` or `q=` is not between `0` and `1`, or `p + q` is not less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} With `p=0` and `q=0`, each of the `98` added nodes brings two edges: ::: {#efa51a44 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_extended_barabasi_albert_graph(n=100, m=2, p=0, q=0, seed=4) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 196) ``` ::: ::: Steps that add edges between existing nodes make the graph denser: ::: {#75619eed .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ ec.Graph() .add_extended_barabasi_albert_graph(n=100, m=2, p=p, q=0.1, seed=4) .count_edges() for p in (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [196, 262, 346, 476] ``` ::: :::
